facts.text: Newbern was originally called Cane Brake because of abundant cane, then renamed after New Bern, North Carolina, the former seat of the British Province.
In 1829, Harvey Tyndall and Simpson Hemphill opened Newbern’s first store, dubbed Grab All, marking the town’s early commercial start.
The 1859 arrival of a railroad from Uniontown linked Newbern to the Selma‑Demopolis line, boosting cotton exports before the Civil War.
Newbern’s historic district is listed on the Alabama Register of Landmarks and History, preserving many 19th‑century structures.
During the Civil War, Newbern supplied soldiers to the Fifth, Eleventh, and Twentieth Alabama regiments, reflecting its deep Confederate ties.
